extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of psychology, psychoanalysis, aesthetics, literary theory, and humor research
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting principles and technical criteria from Freud's essay 'Wit and Its Relation to the Unconscious' to evaluate or produce wit/humor, focusing on linguistic techniques, psychological mechanisms, and social motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: wit_as_playful_judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit characterized as a 'playful judgment'—an aesthetic attitude freed from conventional restrictions; 'wit is a playful judgment' (Lipps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a witticism displays an attitude of aesthetic freedom or 'play'—i.e., a judgment that treats subject matter playfully rather than according to ordinary practical rules. Examples cited: Lipps's account of playful contemplation and Jean Paul's 'free play of ideas.' Anti-pattern: strictly prosaic or didactic remark lacking playful detachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: discovery_of_hidden_similarities_union_of_dissimilarities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to discover or present hidden similarities in dissimilar things (Jean Paul: 'wit is the disguised priest who unites every couple').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for a linking of elements that appear unrelated at first glance, producing surprise through unexpected unity. Example: fusion neologisms that combine disparate concepts. Anti-pattern: comparisons that are obvious or merely tautological.

rubrics_metrics.name: contrast_of_ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit often rests on a contrast or antithesis between ideas—'contrast of ideas' is a common formulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the joke exploits contrast (e.g., meaning vs. meaninglessness, expectation vs. reality). Consider whether the contrast is set up linguistically or conceptually. Anti-pattern: absence of a clear contrasting frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: sense_in_nonsense_confusion_then_clearness
rubrics_metrics.description: Comic/witty effect produced by first ascribing sense to an expression (confusion) and then retracting or resolving it (clearness); 'sense in nonsense' mechanism (Heymans, Lipps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for an initial misleading interpretation followed by immediate clarification or retraction that produces the comic effect (e.g., Heine's 'famillionaire'). Anti-pattern: explanations that arrive too slowly or leave the audience confused rather than amused.

rubrics_metrics.name: brevity_and_ellipsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Brevity is central: 'Brevity alone is the body and soul of wit.' Wit expresses itself in 'too few words' and often leaves things unsaid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the witticism economizes language—omits a clause or compresses meaning so the audience supplies the omitted part. Paraphrase test: if a paraphrase preserves sense but loses laugh-inducing effect, the original's brevity/form was essential. Anti-pattern: long-winded 'explained' jokes that lose spark.

rubrics_metrics.name: unearthing_hidden_or_concealed_elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit must 'unearth something hidden and concealed'—bringing to view a suppressed or latent element (K. Fischer, caricature link).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the witticism exposes a concealed truth, hypocrisy, or hidden aspect of thought/behavior. Social/unmasking jokes often rely on this. Anti-pattern: trivial observations that reveal nothing new.

rubrics_metrics.name: verbal_form_versus_thought_content
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between wit that resides in the thought and wit that resides in form/wording: often the witty character is in the verbal expression rather than the propositional content (paraphrase loses wit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test whether reformulation of the idea in different wording preserves the humor. If not, the technique is formal/linguistic (wordplay, sound, fusion). Anti-pattern: attributing wit solely to content when wording is decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: condensation_with_substitutive_formation_(blend_words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique of fusing two words/ideas into a blended neologism (condensation with substitution) — e.g., 'famillionaire', 'anecdotage', 'Kleptorumania.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For producing/evaluating wit, check for clever blends that compress two propositions into a single word that triggers reconstruction of omitted meaning. Use graphical/morphological analysis to show constituent words. Anti-pattern: awkward or opaque blends that require heavy explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: condensation_with_modification_and_small_change
rubrics_metrics.description: Condensation where a small modification (single letter, reversal, opposite) substitutes and evokes omitted abusive or explanatory content (e.g., 'great future behind him', 'four heels of Achilles').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a minimal linguistic tweak creates an implied secondary thought (often insulting or corrective). The subtler the modification, the stronger the wit. Anti-pattern: heavy-handed changes that feel forced.

rubrics_metrics.name: omission_and_abbreviation_as_technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Compression/abbreviation: omitting a second clause or restraining explicit qualification so the audience reconstructs it; omitted content becomes implicit source of wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the effect of deliberate omission. Good omissions leave trace information enabling reconstructive inference (pleasant surprise). Anti-pattern: omissions that make the utterance ambiguous without yielding a clear humorous resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: pun_and_sound_play
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of puns, sound similarity, word-division and play on words (sound-wit) to create double meanings (double entendre) and ambiguity exploited for comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify homophones, homonyms, or clever word splits that open alternate interpretations. Consider whether the audience can immediately access both readings. Anti-pattern: forced puns that rely on obscure pronunciations.

rubrics_metrics.name: representation_through_opposite_or_contradiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique of representing an idea through its opposite (representation through the opposite) to imply criticism or to provoke surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether phrasing via contradiction or inversion produces ironic insight (e.g., 'great future behind him'). Anti-pattern: inversions that merely state the opposite without clever linkage.

rubrics_metrics.name: succession_of_confusion_and_solution_(riddle_like_mechanism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanism where an enigmatic or nonsensical element first confuses the audience, then is rapidly resolved (enlightenment) producing comic effect (Heine's 'famillionaire' analyzed as confusion→clearness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate temporal structure—does the joke set up an enigma and then resolve it quickly? Timely resolution is crucial; delayed or absent resolution kills the effect. Anti-pattern: unresolved puzzles that produce irritation rather than amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: relation_to_unconscious_and_dream_work_(condensation_displacement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit's linguistic techniques (condensation, displacement) parallel dream-work processes; wit is linked to unconscious mental operations similar to dreams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For analysis, trace how linguistic compressions mirror unconscious condensations/displacements—this supports origin-explanations (why a fused word evokes latent content). Anti-pattern: ignoring the unconscious/work-model when interpreting condensation-based jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: economy_of_psychic_expenditure_as_pleasure_mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleasure of wit arises from an economy of psychic expenditure: wit economizes inhibition, comic economizes thought, humor economizes feeling—these economies produce pleasurable discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluating effect, consider whether the joke reduces psychic cost (e.g., suppresses inhibition, avoids full affective investment) and channels it into pleasurable release. Use this to distinguish wit, comic, and humor. Anti-pattern: treating laughter as purely social without accounting for psychic economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: tendency_wit_or_motivated/hostile_wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit used in the service of tendencies/motives (tendency-wit) such as satire, derision, invective, cynical wit—social and hostile motives shape form and acceptability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess motive: is the wit aiming to attack, unmask, or promote a social tendency? Consider ethical/social consequences and audience alignment. Examples: critical witticisms, cynical jokes, satire. Anti-pattern: ignoring contextual power relations in judging effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: humor_vs_wit_vs_comic_distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish categories: humor (economy of feeling; located in foreconscious), wit (compromise between unconscious and foreconscious; double-facedness), comic (comparison of two modes producing comic difference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify the instance: does it primarily economize affect (humor), hinge on unconscious associations and linguistic trickery (wit), or arise from a perceptual/conceptual comparison (comic)? This classification informs production and interpretation choices. Anti-pattern: conflating categories and missing mechanism-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: use_of_childhood/infantile_material_and_regression
rubrics_metrics.description: Infantile sources (regression) supply material and means for wit/humor—childhood experiences feed the defense processes that wit exploits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the joke leverages infantile memories, wish-fulfillment, or early affective structures; such roots explain some pleasure mechanisms and disarming of affect. Anti-pattern: psychological overreading of every simple pun as infantile without textual support.

rubrics_metrics.name: forms_and_technical_categories_of_wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical/formal categories enumerated as useful taxonomy: sound-wit, play on words, wit of caricature, characterization-wit, witty repartee, word-division, parody, travesty, parody/imitations, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing or evaluating wit, identify which formal category applies and apply category-specific rules (e.g., repartee requires timing and social context; parody requires recognizable source). Anti-pattern: attempting parody without a sufficiently recognizable model.

rubrics_metrics.name: social_process_and_motives_in_wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit as a social process—its transmission, social value (status, fame), and motives (desire to impart wit; social advantage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider social context, audience transmission and the producer's motive (impress, bond, unmask). A witticism's success depends on social uptake and suitability. Anti-pattern: producing technically clever jokes that offend or misfire socially.

rubrics_metrics.name: economized_affect_and_humoristic_displacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor functions as a high-level defense that displaces painful affect and converts readiness for pain into pleasure by deflecting energy to subsidiary matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the humorous device deflects or discharges affect (anger, compassion, fear) into laughter; assess ethical and therapeutic dimensions. Anti-pattern: jokes that exacerbate rather than defuse painful affect.

rubrics_metrics.name: brevity_paraphrase_test_for_linguistic_wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical test: if paraphrase preserves sense but loses the laugh, then the wit is in the wording/technique (brevity and form), not in propositional content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use paraphrase as analytical tool when judging whether effect depends on form. For production, aim for formulations that resist paraphrase without losing clarity. Anti-pattern: relying on explanation to justify a joke's quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: repetition_and_monotony_as_comic_device
rubrics_metrics.description: Repetition and the build-up of monotony can produce comic effect when expectation is subverted by recurrence (Mark Twain's cow-through-roof example: repetition -> eventual meta-commentary produces humor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess timing and accumulation: repeated incidents culminating in a dry remark can convert irritation into humor. Anti-pattern: mere repetition without an achieved meta-commentary or payoff.
